title: Small improvements in the austen_books function?
description:
@juliasilge I really like the janeaustenr package, so many thanks.

I am using it as an example to show that starting with a little "neat" R is often useful.  I have 2 small suggestions:

a) The current version includes the `library(dplyr)` line, but there is no `library(janeaustenr) ` line.  Please could this be added.
b) Your book includes an even "tidier" version with four variables.  Very nice.  Could you include this function instead - or maybe as well?  It is easy to copy from the book, but even easier if it could be included in the package.

```
library(janeaustenr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

original_books <- austen_books() %>%
  group_by(book) %>%
  mutate(linenumber = row_number(),
         chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text, 
                                     regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]",
                                           ignore_case = TRUE)))) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Happy New Year

Roger

title: Error in library(janeaustenr): there is no package called ‘janeaustenr’
description:
When running the first test code in the book "Text Mining With R" I get `Error in library(janeaustenr): there is no package called ‘janeaustenr’`

I followed the install instructions outlined in the book from the URL `https://cran.r-project.org/package=janeaustenr`

I also verified that the library was loaded successfully.  I get the following in my listing of installed packages:
`janeaustenr 1.0.0.9000` 

I also verified (using `??janeaustenr` in my R terminal)  and got:
```
janeaustenr::austen_books
                        Tidy data frame of Jane Austen's 6 completed,
                        published novels
janeaustenr::emma       The text of Jane Austen's novel "Emma"
janeaustenr::janeaustenr
                        janeaustenr: Jane Austen's Complete Novels
  Aliases: janeaustenr, janeaustenr-package
janeaustenr::mansfieldpark
                        The text of Jane Austen's novel "Mansfield
                        Park"
janeaustenr::northangerabbey
                        The text of Jane Austen's novel "Northanger
                        Abbey"
janeaustenr::persuasion
                        The text of Jane Austen's novel "Persuasion"
janeaustenr::prideprejudice
                        The text of Jane Austen's novel "Pride and
                        Prejudice"
janeaustenr::sensesensibility
                        The text of Jane Austen's novel "Sense and
                        Sensibility"
```

Here is the source code I am running. My current version of R is: 4.1.0 on Ubuntu 20.04.

```
library(janeaustenr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

original_books <- austen_books() %>%
  group_by(book) %>%
  mutate(linenumber = row_number(),
         chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text,
                                     regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]",
                                           ignore_case = TRUE)))) %>%
  ungroup()

original_books
```

title: Character encoding is "unknown" but should be "latin1"
description:
Thanks for your work on this package, it's a great resource for people looking for text data analysis examples. Unfortunately, there's a small problem with the encoding for *Mansfield Park*:

```
> Encoding(mansfieldpark[15222])
[1] "UTF-8"

> mansfieldpark[15222]
[1] "the command of her beauty, and her \xa320,000, any one who could satisfy the"
```

The `\xa3` is probably meant to encode a pound sign, [U+00A3](http://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/00A3/index.htm). Note, however, that the UTF-8 encoding of U+00A3 is `\xc2\xa3`. I think the text is probably encoded in Latin-1, where the encoding of U+00A3 is `\xa3`. 

If we set the encoding to "latin1", then we display the correct symbol:
```
> Encoding(mansfieldpark) <- "latin1"

> mansfieldpark[15222]
[1] "the command of her beauty, and her £20,000, any one who could satisfy the"
```
This leads me to believe that the texts are encoded in Latin-1 but declared to be UTF-8. This will cause problems for other packages, including [corpus](https://github.com/patperry/r-corpus), which refuses to process invalid UTF-8.

There are two easy fixes:

1. Set the encoding to Latin-1:

```
Encoding(mansfieldpark) <- "latin1"
```

2. Alternatively, convert the Latin-1 data to UTF-8:

```
mansfieldpark <- iconv(mansfieldpark, "latin1", "UTF-8")
```

If you want to make sure that the conversion worked, you can try `corpus::as_text(mansfieldpark)`, which will fail if the data is invalid. It looks like the other books are all valid UTF-8.
